correctness.rationale: The classification uses the exhaustive scalar, nonzero Jordan nilpotent, and distinct-spectrum cases. Polynomial identities show non-similar originals cannot become similar upon amplifying with a nonzero Hilbert identity. In the Jordan case the ratio of the norms of the nilpotent parts gives a necessary bound attained by diagonal conjugacy. In the distinct-spectrum case the spectral involutions give a necessary operator-norm ratio, attained by an explicit diagonal intertwiner in bisector eigenvector coordinates. All norm comparisons persist under tensoring with any nonzero identity. The tE12 pair attains theta_{2,q}(t)=t. Deterministic checker passed 5200 supplementary assertions, not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The exact two-dimensional cancellation threshold is a natural structural boundary for the 2026 similarity-amplification problem: no Hilbert multiplicity improves optimal conditioning, whereas sufficiently large matrices can improve. The theorem determines all cases with attained constants and supplies an explicit extremal family for every t. This is not just a normalization or routine test; it closes the small-dimension sharp-envelope question and establishes the nontrivial invariant ratio between nonorthogonal eigenbases.
